Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (indicated by arrowheads pointing to the abnormally wide tracheal walls) and diffuse bronchiectasis with cystic changes in the lower lobes. This combination of massive dilation of the trachea and main bronchi is the hallmark radiological feature of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly).
